report.answer: Within the 12–23 hour window, Wednesday 2024-07-31 had 70,674 trips versus Saturday 2024-07-27's 59,736, a 15.5% like-for-like gap after accounting for the 12 shared hours. H1 confirms that even in this shared window, Wednesday consistently outperforms Saturday, indicating intrinsic weekday demand patterns (commuter/business travel) outweigh weekend leisure patterns. H3 further shows that airport trips were proportionally similar (~10%) but absolutely lower on Saturday (6,082 vs 6,900), contributing to the total shortfall but not driving it disproportionately. The raw whole-day gap of -39.2% is partly a data-coverage artefact (missing early morning/late night hours), but a real 15.5% difference persists when comparing the same 12-hour window.

causes.cause: Intrinsic weekday demand pattern: Wednesday attracts more commuter and business travel than Saturday, even within the 12–23 shared window.

rejected_explanations: Weather suppressed Saturday demand (Saturday was clear; Wednesday was rainy, yet Wednesday had more trips).
data_caveats: The 12–23 window excludes early morning (00–11) and late night hours (24+); partial-day coverage differences contribute to the raw whole-day gap of -39.2%, but the like-for-like 12-hour window comparison isolates a real 15.5% difference.
Airport trip percentages are similar (~10%) on both days, suggesting airport effects are proportional rather than a disproportionate driver of the gap.
The trips per hour normalization could not be computed (H4 rejected due to query error), so the exact within-hour rate persistence of the 15.5% gap remains unconfirmed.
report.recommendation: Maintain standard dispatch levels for Saturday evenings within the 12–23 window; the 15.5% gap is driven by weekday vs. weekend travel patterns, not weather or airport volume fluctuations.
limitations: Only two days are compared; no multi-day trend or regression controls for day-of-week or month-over-month effects.
The trips per hour normalization was not computed (H4 rejected due to query error), so the exact within-hour rate persistence of the 15.5% gap remains unconfirmed.
Data caveat: The 12–23 window excludes early morning and late night hours; partial-day coverage differences are acknowledged but excluded from the like-for-like comparison.
